title: Extensionless entrypoints leave every file marked as the wrong language
reasoning: The function explicitly resolves an extensionless entry such as 'main' to 'main.py', but computes entry_extensions before that resolution. It consequently passes None to measure_files, marking all files is_entry_language=False. Updating target_entry_path later enables Python tracing and graph construction but never corrects the language flags, which are then persisted incorrectly.
reproduction: Measure a snapshot containing main.py and helper.py with entry_file='main'. The entry resolves to main.py, but both returned FileMetrics objects have is_entry_language=False, unlike the equivalent call with entry_file='main.py'.
recommendation: Resolve the actual entry file before determining its language and measuring files, then use its language extensions consistently.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included snapshot tests assert language flags only for entry_file values that already include '.py'; none cover the extensionless resolution branch.
suggestedRegressionTest: Extend snapshot measurement scenarios to compare explicit and extensionless entrypoints in a mixed-language snapshot, asserting identical language flags in returned metrics and saved rows.
minimumFixScope: Entry resolution in src/slop_code/metrics/driver.py and existing snapshot measurement tests.

history.reasoning: Both evidence files still exist, but the relevant driver logic moved and now supports the repair: driver.py:81-102 resolves extensionless entrypoints before language selection and measurement at lines 439-445. Language flags are assigned at lines 127-133 and persisted by quality_io.py:75. A regression scenario at tests/metrics/driver_test.py:625 compares explicit and extensionless entrypoints in mixed-language metrics and saved rows.
